messages:
Asha: Quick UX note from usability session: users misinterpret the smoothing toggle as 'noise removal' for anomalies. They thought smoothing would hide spikes permanently. Screenshot of confusion: https://img.redwood.example/ux/smoothing-confuse.png

Marco: That's a problem. Smoothing is just a visual filter, not data transform. We need clearer copy and an explicit "show raw peaks" affordance so users know spikes still exist.

Sam (Design): Agree. Proposal: change toggle label from 'Smoothing' to 'Smoothing (visual only)' and add a secondary micro-link 'Show raw peaks' that overlays hollow markers at raw values when smoothing is on.

Priya: Micro-link must be keyboard-accessible and discoverable. Maybe use a small icon with a tooltip "overlay raw values". Also consider onboarding hint the first time smoothing is toggled.

Asha: During testing, participants also wanted the legend to allow pinning series so they remain visible when toggling smoothing or normalization. Can we add a pin action in the legend (tiny pin icon)?

Marco: Pin makes sense. Implementation: legend entries get a pin button; pinned series get a heavier stroke and persistent hover markers. Unpin reverses. We'll need to define keyboard targets for the pin too.

Sam (Design): Copy for the smoothing tooltip: 'Smoothing: visually averages nearby points to reduce noise. Raw values still available via "Show raw peaks".' Tooltip for pin: 'Pin series: keep visible during filters and toggles.'

a11y-bot: reminder: tooltip content must be exposed via aria-describedby; icon buttons need aria-pressed for pin state and keyboard handlers. Contrast for hollow raw markers must meet 3:1.

Priya: Decision: rename toggle, add 'Show raw peaks' overlay, add legend pin. Action items: Sam  update mock & microcopy; Marco  implement icon + overlay; Asha  run follow-up test. Target: prototype in 1 sprint.

Sam (Design): I'll also draft the one-time onboarding tooltip text.

Asha: Thanks! :thumbsup:
